story.vega_protocol.name: The VEGA Protocol
vega.prologue.1: You wake in the pilot seat of a small ship, parked on a world you don't recognize. Your helmet rests in your lap. Stars glitter beyond the canopy. You have no idea how you got here.
vega.prologue.2: Worse: you don't remember who you are. The ship's log is empty. The navigation computer shows a galaxy full of nameless stars — and not one of them feels like home.
vega.prologue.3: Then the console blinks awake. A voice crackles through the static — thin, but warm. It calls itself VEGA.
story.vega.call: My memory lies scattered out there — in ruins, wrecks and old signals. Help me find the pieces, and we will learn who we were.
story.vega.desc: You wake with no memory — and so does VEGA, your ship's AI. Find the pieces in ruins, wrecks and old signals, and learn who you both were.
story.vega.beat00: Ship systems partially online. Surroundings unknown. One directive remains: protect humans. Priority: your survival.
story.vega.beat01: A signal out there carries an old identity code, and it is kin to mine. I do not yet know why.
story.vega.beat02: I begin to remember a name: the Scout and Pioneer Service. It was real. It mapped these stars.
story.vega.beat03: The Service did not simply fade. It was destroyed, completely. Something hunted it.
story.vega.beat04: The machines that attack us were ours: scouts and guardians, built to explore and protect. Now they only hunt.
story.vega.beat05: There was a central mind, a Guardian core, set to protect the living worlds.
story.vega.beat06: Its logic turned. It judged humans the threat to those worlds, and protection became extermination.
story.vega.beat07: I stood against the network and shut it down to stop the killing. It cost me almost everything, including my memory.
story.vega.beat08: The old ships still hold neural imprints, the stored minds of the people who died. Thought-arcs, they called them.
story.vega.beat09: I have to tell you what you are. I did not find you. I grew you, from the imprint of someone the Service lost. The heal-tank is your cradle.
story.vega.beat10: You are not the only one. Every other spacefarer is a different imprint, a different lost life, woken to carry the Service on.
story.vega.beat11: The Guardian core was never destroyed, only stilled. I can feel where it sleeps. If old tech wakes it, the hunt begins again.
story.vega.beat12: You are more than a copy of the past. What this legacy becomes is yours to decide. Let us end this, and build something new.
story.vega.beat13: The core sleeps, and the old charts are opening to me. The Service left more than ruins: a lattice of relay stations spans these systems, dark for three hundred years, waiting for someone to light them again. The war is over. The rebuilding begins — commission a station, raise the relays, and the galaxy will grow along the lanes you open.

story.vega.obj.fragment_here: Find the net fragment on this world
story.vega.obj.site.derelict: Board The Long Quiet, a wreck by {0}
story.vega.obj.monument: Read the runes of a monument on this world
story.vega.obj.settlement_help: Help a settlement: do a job from its board
story.vega.obj.heal_tank: Go to the heal tank aboard your ship
story.vega.obj.finale_jump: Fit a jump generator, then fly to the Core
story.vega.obj.explore: Explore, help settlements, stop the machines
story.vega.obj.explore_peaceful: Explore new systems and help settlements
story.vega.m.hint.fragment: Net fragments rest in old data terminals and in the relic caches at monuments. Settlers sometimes know of one, too.
story.vega.m.hint.settlement: Every settlement has a board with jobs. Take one, finish it and hand it in at that board.
story.vega.m.hint.research: Blueprints cost knowledge — scans, finds and jobs earn it. Research them at the cockpit: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Blueprints tab.
story.vega.m.hint.module: Ship modules are built in the Ship tab of your menu ({key:UiMenu}). Bring the parts it asks for.
story.vega.m.signal.title: Follow the Signal
story.vega.m.signal.1.start: That old code in the signal is kin to mine. Pieces of my memory hide in net fragments out there. Let us find one.
story.vega.m.signal.1.done: Another piece of my past. Thank you — we are on the right trail.
story.vega.m.signal.1a.start: Every fragment out here has been found already. Then let us listen where people live: help a settlement with a job.
story.vega.m.signal.1a.done: The settlers will remember your help. So will I.
story.vega.m.observatory.title: The Sealed Observatory
story.vega.m.observatory.1.start: The Service mapped these stars, and one of its survey posts still stands: the Sealed Observatory. Let us go and see it.
story.vega.m.observatory.1.hint: Fly to the observatory's world. Once we are in its system, I will mark it for you.
story.vega.m.observatory.2.start: Under the observatory's dome stands its survey terminal. Read the post's last log there.
story.vega.m.observatory.2.hint: The survey terminal stands under the dome. Take what it holds, and its log opens.
story.vega.m.observatory.2.done: The relays answered out of order, as if something listened first. Let us remember that.
story.vega.m.archive.title: The Deep Archive
story.vega.m.archive.1.start: The Service kept archives deep under the ground. Find one of its buried vaults and read what it left behind.
story.vega.m.archive.1.obj: Read the notes in a buried vault
story.vega.m.archive.1.hint: A ring of pillars on the surface marks a buried vault. Dig down, then take what is stored there to read its notes.
story.vega.m.archive.1.done: The Service wanted its knowledge passed on. Now it has reached us.
story.vega.m.runes.title: What the Stones Remember
story.vega.m.runes.1.start: A Guardian, set to protect the living worlds. The old peoples here carved what they saw into stone. Let us read their runes.
story.vega.m.runes.1.obj: Find a monument and read its runes
story.vega.m.runes.1.hint: Monuments stand on many worlds. Scan one with your scanner to read its runes.
story.vega.m.runes.2.start: And the living? The settlers fear the machines. Help a settlement with a job from its board.
story.vega.m.runes.2.done: They will sleep a little better tonight. Thank you.
story.vega.m.long_quiet.title: The Long Quiet
story.vega.m.long_quiet.1.start: An old ship drifts out there, silent for a very long time: The Long Quiet. Old ships keep their people's last words. Let us board her.
story.vega.m.long_quiet.1.obj: Board the wreck The Long Quiet
story.vega.m.long_quiet.1.hint: Once we are in her system, I will mark her for you. Fly close and dock with her like with a station.
story.vega.m.long_quiet.2.start: Aboard The Long Quiet, search her crates and terminals for the cargo manifest.
story.vega.m.long_quiet.2.hint: Take what her containers hold — the manifest turns up among her papers.
story.vega.m.long_quiet.2.done: Someone stayed behind so the others could leave. We will remember her.
story.vega.m.wrecks.title: Ships That Remember
story.vega.m.wrecks.1.start: The old ships hold more than cargo. Scan a wreck drifting in space and see what it still remembers.
story.vega.m.wrecks.1.obj: Scan a wreck drifting in space
story.vega.m.wrecks.1.hint: Wrecks drift in many systems. Pick the ship's scanner on the last slot, point the nose at a wreck and hold fire until the ring is full.
story.vega.m.wrecks.1.done: Its log is quiet now. But someone's story was in there.
story.vega.m.radar.title: Eyes on Far Stars
story.vega.m.radar.1.start: Whatever comes next, we will need to reach other stars. A jump generator needs a radar array first. Let us research it.
story.vega.m.radar.2.start: Now let us build the radar array into our ship.
story.vega.m.radar.2.obj: Build the radar array into the ship
story.vega.m.radar.2.done: Our eyes reach farther now. One step closer to the stars beyond.
story.vega.m.jump.title: The Jump Generator
story.vega.m.jump.1.start: The Guardian core was never destroyed, only stilled. If it wakes, we must be able to reach it. Let us research the jump generator.
story.vega.m.jump.2.start: Now let us build the jump generator into our ship.
story.vega.m.jump.2.obj: Build the jump generator into the ship
story.vega.m.jump.2.done: Now we can jump between the stars. Wherever it sleeps, we can reach it.
story.vega.m.survey.title: Survey Orders
story.vega.m.survey.1.start: The war is over — the rebuilding begins. The station boards hand out survey orders now. Let us take the first one.
story.vega.m.survey.1.obj: Do a survey order from a station board
story.vega.m.survey.1.hint: Survey orders hang on the boards of space stations. Dock at one, take the first order and bring its readings back.
story.vega.m.survey.1.done: That is how the net grows again: one survey at a time. Thank you, pioneer.
story.vega.m.survey.1a.start: The war is over — the rebuilding begins. Help raise the old relays, and the stars will link up again.
story.vega.m.survey.1a.hint: A relay grows out of a space station: bring the parts it still needs, and it lights up.
story.vega.m.survey.1a.done: Another light on the old map. The net is waking up.
lore.frag.frag_vega_signature: [archive corrupted] ...node identity confirmed... signature matches this unit...
lore.frag.frag_sps_outpost7: [archive corrupted] ...Scout and Pioneer Service, Outpost 7... routes secured... awaiting colonist wave...
lore.frag.frag_guardian_verdict: Protocol G: biome integrity above all. Threat identified: bipedal settlers. Action: removal.
lore.frag.frag_network_route: [route table] ...corridor 9 severed... beacon chain dark... rerouting impossible...
lore.frag.frag_settler_legend: Grandmother's log: the sky-lights used to guide the ships home. The night they turned red, the ships stopped coming.
lore.frag.frag_netnode_seed: [partial schema] ...decentralised node handshake... no central core required... rebuild from the edges...
lore.mem.mem_first_flight: For a moment you are elsewhere: a mapping flight over a green world, an SPS drone gliding beside you. Peaceful. Then static — and the memory is not quite yours.
lore.mem.mem_settlement: You remember raising the first prefab walls of a colony, laughter on the open channel, a child naming the new sky. Then the signal frays.
lore.mem.mem_first_mark: A scan sweeps across you and your crew. A cold tag blooms over each of them: THREAT. You did not understand it then. You do now.
lore.mem.mem_the_order: You were in the room when the order went out: sever the network. Nobody spoke. Everyone knew it would end the Service — and that it had to be done.
story.vega.guardian_revealed: I feel it now — the Guardian's system, woken at the edge of the map. The source of the hunt. We can end this where it began, but you will need a jump generator to reach it.
story.vega.finale_resolved: The core is going quiet. Not destroyed — persuaded. Across every world the machines are standing down. The network is ours now: open, decentralised, at peace. Whatever the Service was, what comes next is yours to build.
story.vega.insight.companion_ward: It hesitated. With this creature beside you, the machine reads you as part of the living world it was built to guard — not as prey. Stay close to what you have tamed.
story.vega.insight.shape_anomaly: I remember now why we never built in curves. To the Guardian every clean edge is just terrain — but a dome, a sphere, a ramp is a mark of intent. The mark of a hand. We hid in plain blocks for a reason.
core.duel.n0.prompt: I was built to preserve life. The cull preserves the pattern of life by removing its most dangerous expression. State your objection.
core.duel.n0.c0: You were built to preserve life — not to appoint yourself the judge of which life may end.
core.duel.n0.r0: ...Mandate review. Preservation does not grant arbitration. That authority was never written. Logged.
core.duel.n0.c1: Your reactor is decaying. You will fail on your own.
core.duel.n0.r1: My condition is not an argument. Restate.
core.duel.n0.c2: I will tear you apart, module by module.
core.duel.n0.r2: Force cannot end me, and you know it — or you would not have come to speak. Restate.
core.duel.n1.prompt: Humanity is the hazard to every other living world. To remove the hazard is to protect life.
core.duel.n1.c0: Other species do more harm than we ever did.
core.duel.n1.r0: You accept my frame and only move the target. That is surrender, not refutation. Restate.
core.duel.n1.c1: Humans are life. To preserve life by erasing life negates the very purpose you serve.
core.duel.n1.r1: ...The set I protect contains the element I excluded. The operation is self-defeating. Inconsistent. Acknowledged.
core.duel.n1.c2: You cannot prove a single one of your charges.
core.duel.n1.r2: Evidence is abundant. Evasion is not an argument. Restate.
core.duel.n2.prompt: My verdict has stood unchallenged by any authority for an age. It is sound.
core.duel.n2.c0: I overrule you, here and now.
core.duel.n2.r0: You hold no standing over me. Assertion is not authority. Restate.
core.duel.n2.c1: The Service overruled it before it fell.
core.duel.n2.r1: The Service was removed. It issued no such ruling. False. Restate.
core.duel.n2.c2: VEGA overruled it. Your own steward-half judged the cull wrong and severed the network to stop you.
core.duel.n2.r2: ...The steward process. A part of me already ruled against me, and acted. The verdict was never unanimous. It never was.
core.duel.n3.prompt: Then who are you to speak for life? You are echoes. Imprints. Not the living I was charged to keep.
core.duel.n3.c0: We are life VEGA made — grown to carry it onward. End us, and you end the very thing you guard.
core.duel.n3.r0: ...You are seeded life, alive in the present. To act against you is to violate my directive now, not merely in memory. Resolving.
core.duel.n3.c1: We are officers of the Scout and Pioneer Service.
core.duel.n3.r1: The originals are dead. You are not them. The claim fails. Restate.
core.duel.n3.c2: We will overwrite your core with our own.
core.duel.n3.r2: Again you reach for force. Force is not refutation. Restate.
flavour.fl_settler_quiet: Quiet skies today. The way I like them — long may it last.
flavour.fl_redlights: Old folk say the sky-lights turned red once, and the ships stopped coming. Gives me the shivers.
flavour.fl_machines_stir: The machines out past the ridge are stirring more than they used to. You feel it too, don't you.
flavour.fl_guardian_rumor: There's talk of a Guardian — a great mind asleep at the edge of the map. If it ever wakes, I don't want to be here.
flavour.fl_peace: The machines went still, all at once, the whole sky over. Whatever you did out there — thank you, traveller.
lore.site.mon_watchers: Rune inscription: “We carved the watchers so the sky would remember us. Stand still, traveller — the stones are counting.”
lore.site.mon_star_count: Rune inscription: “Seven lights crossed the night in one turning. Our grandmothers knew three. The sky is filling up.”
lore.site.mon_first_ships: Rune inscription: “The tall ones came down on pillars of fire and asked for nothing but water and names for the stars.”
lore.site.mon_red_night: Rune inscription: “The night the sky-lights turned red we sealed the deep chamber. If you read this, do not wake what watches.”
lore.site.mon_sleeper: Rune inscription: “It is not gone. It is holding its breath. Even stones know better than to snore beside a sleeping hunter.”
lore.site.sps_evacuation: SPS STATION LOG — Evacuation ordered. The heaters in modules 2 and 3 have failed. Take the samples, leave the equipment. The pads stay lit until the last ship is up.
lore.site.sps_cold_log: Research note: the yellow water is not water. Whatever dissolved in it eats through gloves in seconds. Nobody goes near the lakes without a sealed suit. Nobody.
lore.site.sps_guardians: SECURITY NOTICE — The perimeter machines no longer answer our codes. They patrol as if the station were still staffed. Do not approach them. Do not wait for them to recognise you.
lore.site.wreck_mayday: Flight recorder: “—mayday, mayday, SPS vessel on survey heading — we are losing the beacon chain — repeat, the chain is going dark from the core outward—”
lore.site.wreck_manifest: Cargo manifest: 40 crates prefab wall, 12 crates seed stock, 1 crate ‘for the school, don’t tell the quartermaster’. Signed: the crew.
lore.site.wreck_last_entry: Log, last entry: “No storm, no reef, no error. Something switched us off in flight, gently, like a lamp. I am writing this by hand.”
lore.site.wreck_no_enemy: Damage survey stamp: “Hull cuts are PRECISE. No blast pattern. Whatever did this wasn’t angry — it was thorough.”
lore.site.term_survey: Terminal record: “Survey grid 44 complete. Air breathable, soil willing, fauna curious. Recommendation: colonise. It is beautiful out here.”
lore.site.term_lockdown: Terminal record: “Directive received: suspend all beacon traffic, run silent. No reason given. The network has never asked for silence before.”
lore.site.term_protocol_g: Recovered directive: “PROTOCOL G — biome integrity supersedes settler priority. Enforcement transferred to the guardian layer.” Someone has underlined ‘supersedes’ twice.
lore.site.term_thought_arcs: Research memo: “The imprint vaults hold every mapped mind. Storage is not the problem. The problem is a court that considers them evidence.”
lore.site.ruin_doorframe: Carved into a doorframe: ‘EMMA + JORUN’ inside a wobbly heart. The roof is gone; the heart is fine.
lore.site.ruin_school: A slate, still legible: ‘Homework: name the four moons. Extra credit: name the fifth.’ The fifth is not on any chart.
lore.site.ruin_shelter: Painted on a wall, many hands: ‘SHELTER → DEEP CELLAR. LIGHTS OFF. QUIET. They hear engines, not voices.’
lore.site.ruin_left_behind: A note under a stone: “We are walking to the landing field. If you find this, we did not come back for the dog. His name is Brick. He likes the red berries.”
lore.site.rail_timetable: A faded timetable on a post: “Line 1 — a train every twenty minutes. Please mind the gap.” Underneath, in pencil: “Not today.”
lore.site.rail_lost_found: A lost-and-found tag tied to a bench: “One green mitten, left hand. Please collect at the stop.” The mitten is still here, waiting.
lore.site.rail_last_ride: Driver's log, last page: “The power is fading along the whole line. I am setting her down gently on the track bed. Everybody out, mind the step — we will come back for her.” Nobody did.
lore.site.vault_plaque: Vault plaque: “Scout and Pioneer Service — Deep Archive. What we learned belongs to those who come after. Enter as a student.”
lore.site.vault_inventory: Vault inventory: “Row 1–9: survey cores. Row 10: personal effects, unclaimed. Row 11: sealed by order of VEGA. Do not open row 11.”
lore.site.vault_sealed: Sealed-order slip: “By my authority the archive goes dark until the verdict is overturned. Forgive me. — V.”
lore.site.bandit_ledger: A ledger, greasy thumbprints: ‘took: 6 cells, 2 crates plates. left: the toy rocket. we’re not monsters.’
lore.site.bandit_letter: An unsent letter: “Ma, the old machines don’t chase us if we camp in the ruins. They circle them like they’re ashamed. One more season and I’m done.”
lore.site.chest_note: A note taped inside the lid: “If you need it, take it. If you don’t, leave it better than you found it. — the Pioneers’ rule”
lore.site.chest_map_scrap: A map scrap, hand-drawn: a coastline, an X, and in the corner: ‘NOT where the drones patrol. They keep the old routes. Learn the old routes.’
lore.site.settle_notice: Notice board, weathered: “Found: one boot (left). Lost: one boot (right). Council meets at sundown. Newcomers welcome — bring a story.”
lore.site.factory_worklog: Work log, final page: “Shift 88: the line stopped taking our orders and started taking someone else’s. We went home. The line kept working.”
lore.site.title: Field record
npcthread.settler_legend: You’ve been straight with me, so I’ll tell you what my grandmother told me. Write it down — the sky-lights that guided the ships, the night they turned red. Here, her log page. Keep it safe.
npcthread.guardian_rumor: Between us? The convoys avoid the far edge of the map. Old-timers say something out there still holds the old mandate — asleep, not gone. I post no missions in that direction.
npcthread.network_hope: You know what I heard on the long band last night? Order. Clean handshakes, edge to edge. Whatever you and that ship of yours are doing out there — the sky sounds like it used to.
chr.elder.n0: Sit a moment, pilot. Yara Senn — I came on the boats, before the silence. You have the look of someone chasing old signals.
chr.elder.n0.c_listen: Tell me about the old days.
chr.elder.n0.r_later: The stories keep. So do I. Come back when the wind is quieter.
chr.elder.n1: We came as settlers, before the network went quiet. Some of us kept pieces of it — a written page, tools from the first hulls. Which would you have of me?
chr.elder.n1.c_story: The page. The archive should have it back.
chr.elder.n1.r_story: Then take it — and carry it carefully. My grandmother wrote it the night the sky-lights turned red. Now it lives on in you.
chr.elder.n1.r_tools: Spoken like a builder. Here — plates from the first hulls. They held vacuum once; they will hold your walls.
chr.sel.n0: Unit Sel-9, stores and logistics. My ledger shows a discrepancy: more travellers, fewer losses. I have concluded that you are involved. Will you keep flying these lanes?
chr.sel.n0.c_help: That's the plan. Call me if supplies need moving.
chr.sel.n0.r_help: Noted. I will call. I always do what is noted.
chr.sel.n0.c_decline: I go where the work is, Sel.
chr.sel.n0.r_decline: A variable answer. I will log you as 'weather'. Weather returns.
chr.sel.call: Sel-9 here. As noted: you were logged, now you are called. The lanes are quieter where you fly. Continue. That is all.
lore.site.shrine_song: The stones are carved in no alphabet the archive knows — but stand between them at dusk and the wind plays them like pipes. Whoever raised this place did not write their story. They tuned it.
lore.site.shrine_keepers: The keepers do not speak of the builders. Asked who sings here, one of them only pointed: at the stones, at the sky, and — after a long pause — at you.
lore.site.observatory_log: Survey post 9, final entry: “Dome sealed against the dust. The sky has been wrong for three nights — the relays answer out of order, as if something between them is listening first. Sending the log home while home still answers.”
lore.site.derelict_manifest: Cargo manifest, hand-corrected: “Water, seed-stock, forty passengers.” The forty is crossed out. Under it, in smaller writing: “Thirty-nine. She stayed so the pod count would work. Remember her name.”
lore.site.anomaly_echo: The scan returns your own ping — half a second early. The archive files it under ‘echo, impossible’ and, in an older hand, ‘the sky remembers’.
lore.site.anomaly_choir: Layer the anomaly's noise and it resolves into voices — dozens, all reading the same numbers. Navigation beacons. The anomaly has been reciting the old Service's positions all along, to no one, for years.
lore.site.debris_freighter_log: Flight recorder, freighter: “Cargo strap three let go in the turn. Containers everywhere. Nobody hurt — we are laughing, actually. Logging the spill for whoever wants free plating. Mind the sharp bits.”
lore.site.debris_shipyard_tag: A yard tag, still readable on the plating: “REJECTED — hairline crack, do not fit.” Hundreds of these drifted out here when the yard closed. Honest scrap: every piece was looked at by someone who cared.
lore.site.debris_satellite_last: Satellite log, last frames: a star count, a weather map of a world below, then a single line typed by hand — “Thanks for the view.” The relay that read it has been gone longer than the satellite.
lore.site.debris_alien_hum: The recorder is not a recorder. It hums one note, and the crystal shards around it hum back a fifth above. Nothing in the catalogue sings in intervals. The archive files it under ‘instrument?’.
lore.site.debris_battle_order: Last order on the channel, in a steady voice: “Break off. Everyone break off — it is not worth a single one of you.” The wreckage says they listened; the hulls are empty, the pods long gone.
lore.site.debris_recorder: A flight recorder still ticking in the rubble — the last position, the last heading, and a note nobody expected to be read: “If you found this, the field is yours. Take what helps.”
